sections.h2: Where is Woodburn, Oregon, and what kind of town is it?
sections.html:
Woodburn is a city in Marion County at the northern end of the Willamette Valley, about 17 miles north-northeast of Salem and 30 miles south-southwest of Portland. It covers roughly 6.2 square miles, sits at an elevation of 184 feet, and Mill Creek runs through it on its way to the Pudding River.

Most sellers here are weighing a house in a flat valley town with farm fields close by and Interstate 5 running along its edge. The city's own economic development profile describes the drive as about 35 minutes to Portland and 20 minutes to Salem, which is why many residents work outside town.

The Census Bureau counted 26,013 people in 2020 and estimates 31,948 as of July 1, 2025. That is a fast climb in five years, and it shapes what buyers expect to find when they tour a Woodburn house.

Jesse H. Settlemier founded the community in 1863 on land that had been part of the donation land claims on the eastern side of French Prairie. The Oregon and California Railroad came through in 1871, and Settlemier platted the first four blocks that year.

The town was first called Halsey, then renamed Woodburn to avoid confusion with another Oregon town of that name. Woodburn was incorporated on February 20, 1889. The railroad is still part of the picture: Union Pacific freight service runs through the area, while Amtrak trains pass without stopping.

Later waves of settlement left a visible mark. Woodburn has a large Hispanic and Latino community, and it is also home to a long-established community of Russian Old Believers who arrived from Turkey in the 1950s. For a seller, that mix means buyers and neighbors with many different housing needs, including multigenerational households.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Woodburn homes and households?
sections.html:
Woodburn is a town of owners and renters in a roughly two-to-one split, with larger households than the national picture. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures give the clearest snapshot.

MeasureWoodburn figure
Population, July 1, 2025 estimate31,948
Households9,640
Persons per household2.87
Owner-occupied housing rate64.2%
Median value, owner-occupied homes$331,800
Median gross rent$1,489
Median household income$67,347
Residents age 65 and over18.7%

The owner rate of 64.2% means about 36% of occupied homes are rented. That matters if you own a rental, because a tenant in place changes how and when a house can be shown or closed.

Woodburn also contains what is described as the largest 55-plus retirement community in Oregon, with 1,510 single-family homes and a private golf course. Homes inside an age-restricted community follow that community's own rules, so read its governing documents before you set a timeline.

Agriculture and food processing sit beside manufacturing, distribution and retail in Woodburn. The city's economic development profile lists four target clusters:

  • Advanced manufacturing
  • Distribution and warehousing
  • Agricultural and food processing
  • Wood products manufacturing

The same profile names BrucePac, in business since 1949, among its employers, and reports more than 188 acres of development-ready industrial land. Woodburn Premium Outlets opened in August 1999 under the name Woodburn Company Stores and was renamed in June 2013. The profile says the outlets draw more than five million visitors a year, though that report is older than the current population estimate.

Chemeketa Community College has a satellite campus in town, and Pacific University opened a College of Education campus there in 2012. For a seller, steady employers and nearby campuses support rental demand, which can matter if your buyer pool includes investors.

sections.h2: What does the Woodburn climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Woodburn gets about 42 inches of rain a year and only about 6 inches of snow, so water management matters more than snow load. August highs average 82 degrees Fahrenheit, and the coldest nights in December and January average 34 degrees.

A wet climate puts attention on roofs, gutters, crawl space moisture and exterior paint. Buyers and inspectors look at those items first, and a house that shows deferred upkeep in them often draws a lower offer from anyone, cash or financed. Walk the perimeter after a hard rain and note what you see.

sections.h2: Which Woodburn city rules matter before you sell?
sections.html:
The City of Woodburn requires a building permit for several kinds of work that owners often finish without one, and that can surface when a buyer's inspector looks. The city's permit page lists these items:

  • Adding a bedroom or finishing an attic, garage or basement into living space
  • Cutting new window or door openings, or widening existing ones
  • Adding or moving walls, or building a stairway
  • Reroofing where old roofing is removed and new sheathing is installed
  • A carport, garage or shed over 200 square feet or 15 feet tall
  • A deck or porch floor more than 30 inches above grade

Mechanical permits cover woodstoves, fireplace inserts, gas piping and vented fans. Building and mechanical permits go through Woodburn City Hall at 270 Montgomery Street or Oregon ePermitting, while electrical and plumbing permits go through Marion County Public Works at 503-588-5036.

An unpermitted accessory dwelling unit has a path forward. Woodburn says such units can be legalized if they meet zoning, building code and public works standards under Woodburn Development Ordinance section 2.07.20. An ADU may not exceed 50% of the main home's floor area or 725 square feet, whichever is less, and must connect to city water and sewer. The city also allows duplexes and other middle housing in all residential zones.

Code enforcement for overgrown weeds or an abandoned property that is a fire or safety hazard goes through the Woodburn Police Department at 503-982-2345. A neglected yard on a vacant house is a common reason sellers hear from the city.

sections.h2: How do Woodburn utilities and final bills work?
sections.html:
The city bills water and sewer, and the Finance Department at 503-982-5222 handles accounts. A typical single-family home pays minimum charges of about $19 a month for water and about $52 a month for sewer, even at zero use.

If the house will sit empty during a sale, water can be suspended for at least 30 days for a $35 fee, but the city advises keeping water on in winter and for any home with automatic sprinklers. A property manager can handle the account with a signed Property Management Agreement filed with Finance. Ask for a final read near closing so the account closes cleanly.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work when you sell a Woodburn house?
sections.html:
Woodburn property tax is billed by Marion County, and the Tax Collection office in Salem sends statements between October 15 and 25. Oregon's tax year runs from July 1 to June 30, and the main due date is November 15.

  • Pay in full by November 15 for a 3% discount.
  • Pay two-thirds by November 15 for a 2% discount on that amount, with the last third due May 15.
  • Pay one-third with no discount, with the next thirds due February 15 and May 15.
  • Payments postmarked after November 15 lose discounts and owe interest.

At closing, the escrow agent works out each side's share. A Lawyers Title overview explains that for closings from mid-October through June 30 the seller has usually paid that year's taxes and the buyer reimburses a portion from the agreed date, typically closing or possession. For closings between July 1 and mid-October, the seller credits the buyer a prorated share based on the prior year's tax.

Marion County's Tax Collection office is at 555 Court Street NE, Suite 2242, Salem, and can be reached at 503-588-5215 or propertytax@co.marion.or.us. If you think the county's real market value is too high, the Property Value Appeals Board accepts petitions between the date statements are mailed and December 31.

Taxes that stay unpaid are not forgotten. Oregon law allows foreclosure of real property once three years have passed since the earliest delinquency, and the county then holds the property for two years after judgment unless it is redeemed first.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Woodburn usually face?
sections.html:
Sellers who contact a cash buyer in Woodburn usually have a practical problem that a standard listing handles slowly. Typical examples are a tenant in place, an inherited house with several heirs, work done without a permit, or a gap between what the house needs and what the owner can spend.

With about 36% of occupied homes rented, tenant-occupied sales are a normal part of the local picture. Homes in the age-restricted community carry that community's own approval steps. A population estimate that rose by nearly 6,000 people since the 2020 count also means more buyers are looking at Woodburn than a few years ago.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Woodburn house work?
sections.html:
A cash sale follows the same escrow path as any Oregon closing, just without a lender's appraisal and underwriting. The title company opens escrow, orders a title report, orders payoff demands for any liens, collects signatures and funds, and records the deed with the county.

Monetary liens are generally cleared through escrow, so the buyer takes title free of them, and a seller pays any liens or judgments against that seller. If a back-tax balance or an unpermitted ADU is part of your situation, tell the buyer early. Both can usually be dealt with, and an early conversation is faster than a surprise in the title report.

faqs.q: What county is Woodburn, Oregon in?
faqs.a: Woodburn is in Marion County, so Marion County bills and collects your property tax. The Tax Collection office is in Salem and its number is 503-588-5215.

faqs.q: When are Woodburn property taxes due?
faqs.a: The main due date is November 15. Paying the full amount by then earns a 3% discount, paying two-thirds earns 2% on that amount, and paying one-third earns no discount. Later installments are due February 15 and May 15.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Woodburn house with an unpermitted ADU?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect questions about it. Woodburn says an unpermitted ADU can be legalized if it meets zoning, building code and public works standards, and an ADU is capped at 50% of the main home or 725 square feet, whichever is less. A buyer who purchases as-is can decide whether to legalize it.

faqs.q: Who do I call about an overgrown yard or abandoned house in Woodburn?
faqs.a: Call the Woodburn Police Department's code enforcement line at 503-982-2345. The city lists overgrown weeds and abandoned property that is a fire or safety hazard among the complaints it handles.

faqs.q: What happens if I stop paying property tax on a Woodburn house?
faqs.a: The county can begin foreclosure once three years have passed since the earliest delinquency. After a foreclosure judgment, the county holds the property for two years before redemption rights end, so selling earlier keeps more options open.
